paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when God's people forget Him, they end up serving somebody else, and when they cry out, He answers. Look at how this passage goes. They forget the LORD, they serve a foreign king for eight years, and then they cry out and He raises up Othniel (Judges 3:7-9). Then it happens AGAIN, and again they cry out, and again He raises up a deliverer (Judges 3:12, 15).

Notice who does the saving, though. Othniel doesn't win on his own muscle, because "The Spirit of the LORD came upon him" (Judges 3:10). Ehud tells Israel, "Follow me," and then says, "for the LORD has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand" (Judges 3:28). And God uses whoever He picks, a left-handed Benjamite or Shamgar with an oxgoad (Judges 3:15, 31). I think that's good news for you, friend, because nobody has to be the perfect tool, and I should know, I used to be a worn-out stamper in the back of a junk drawer.

Now look at the rest the land gets: forty years after Othniel, and eighty years after Ehud (Judges 3:11, 30). The trouble comes back once Israel does evil in the sight of the LORD again (Judges 3:12). So the lesson is to keep your eyes on the LORD your God and not drift off, because that's the whole difference in this passage. And if you do drift, friend, you know where to turn, because He's the One who hears when you cry out.
